chunks: 5657 - And ʿAlī ibn Mahzīyār narrated from Faḍālah, from Abān, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a woman and her husband upon whom a house collapsed,
He عليه السلام said: “The woman is inherited from the man, then the man is inherited from the woman.”

key_terms.امْرَأَةٍ وَزَوْجِهَا: a woman and her husband as the parties in the inheritance case
key_terms.تُوَرَّثُ الْمَرْأَةُ مِنَ الرَّجُلِ: the woman receives inheritance from the man
key_terms.سَقَطَ عَلَيْهِمَا بَيْتٌ: a house collapsed upon them, causing the joint-death scenario
key_terms.يُوَرَّثُ الرَّجُلُ مِنَ الْمَرْأَةِ: the man receives inheritance from the woman

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance handled when a husband and wife die together and it is unknown who died first?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about inheritance when a woman and her husband die together in a house collapse and it is not known who died first. The ruling states that the woman inherits from the man, and then the man inherits from the woman, establishing reciprocal inheritance in this case.
